item.title: Opposition rejects Marape’s Cash for “Criminals” Scheme; Applies Eson test to gun Buy-back
item.description: The Deputy Leader of the Opposition Keith Iduhu, MP, has today formally rejected the Marape-Rosso Government’s proposed National Firearms Amnesty and Buy-Back Program, labelling it an ethical failure and a dangerous "payday for criminals." Applying the Opposition’s ESON Framework (Em Stret, O Nogat?), Iduhu scrutinised the 21-day program set to begin on February 27, 2026, and delivered a scathing assessment of the government's approach to national security.
